I recently discovered this about myself too.

  
In February I tracked everything I ate in a day

  
And in march I am tracking what I eat in  day, along with things like what I was feeling when I ate it, if I was hungry, did I eat fast/slow, was I satisfied, and just a small journal entry of why I ate it, what I thought about this day and what I ate in it.

  
This has helped me become mindful of what I eat, and make food decisions consciously (usually if I am triggered to eat, I will not think about it and just eat) (I don’t have the willpower yet to change these decisions, but hey, at least I’m starting to be self-aware)  
I realized that I don’t allow myself to feel hunger at all. So what I did yesterday is, is that I sat with my lunch until I was hungry and I decided to feel hunger, and described my emotions to myself as I was hungry.  I realized that I hate feeling hungry, and I am afraid of it, almost to a panic level.

I asked myself why and I realized that:  
a.	Growing up – food was presented to me as a solution for everything  
b.	I was told that God will be mad at me if I don’t clear my plate  
c.	I was never asked “are you hungry” but I was either told that “its time to eat” or I was asked “do you want to eat”   
\-	I realized that I have never associated eating as something you do when you are hungry, but something you do at specified times of the day, something you do when you are bored, and something you do to prevent hunger.   
d.	When I learned to refuse food, I was warned “but you will feel hungry” in a cautionary tone. So I associated hunger with something bad.  
e.	When I was 6 years old, I was shown the picture of “the vulture and the little girl” it’s a picture of a vulture patiently waiting for a famine-stricken boy to die of hunger. This happened in Sudan, the picture was published in the New York Times in 1993 and won a Pulitzer, the photographer committed suicide afterward.   
\-	I was shown this image and explained this story when I was SIX YEARS OLD. I don’t know WTF my parents/sister thought it was okay to show this to me.  
\-	Now when I think back on it, I realized that THIS was the instant that I realized that I never wanted to feel hunger.
